In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of human monoclonal (HMAb) in mice and the factors affecting the production.
the development of a method to obtain human monoclonal MAbs from human lymph node lymphoma patients.
the production of human monoclonal IgM and IgG antibodies in SCID mouse peritoneal ascites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production of human MAb in the SCID mouse ascitic fluid is influenced by many factors, including the hybridoma cell line, the mouse strain, the immunosuppressant, and the antibiotic used.

pristane and HAT selection of human-mouse hybridoma cells are important in the successful production of human MAbs in the mouse ascitic form, that the use of anti-asialo serum has no significant effect on this production, and that antibiotics have a differential effect depending on the HAT selection of the hybridoma cell lines.

the effects of the immunosuppressant pristane and the antibiotics penicillin G, streptomycin and kanamycin on the production of human MAb in SCID mouse heterohybridoma ascites are variable, and that the effects depend on the individual hybridoma and the conditions of the hybridoma culture in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of pristane pretreated SCID mice for the propagation of human-mouse heterhybridomas in ascites is generally effective and that the use of antibiotics is not necessary.
the pristane pretreatments were effective in enhancing the MAb production in all five of the heterohybridomas, but the antibiotics enhanced the production only in two of the four hybridomas.
pristane pretreated heterohybridomas produced MAb in the ascites of SCID mice and that the production was further increased by the co-injection with antibiotics of the hybridomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of pristane pretreated SCID mice is essential to achieve a high level of MAb production by heterohybridomas, and the use of antibiotics is beneficial for some hybridomas but not others.
the effects of pristane pretreatments and the effects of the co-injection with antibiotics on MAb production are different for the two types of hybridomas.

pristane pretreated SCID mice can support the production of human MAb by heterohybridomas, but the production is enhanced by antibiotics only when the hybridomas are propagated in HAT medium, suggesting that the effect of antibiotics is mediated by their inhibition of bacterial contamination.
